title: Synthetic stepped-load TPS benchmark and p95 regression detector
creator: Maya Kline
description: Build a deterministic synthetic stepped-load tokens-per-second (TPS) microbenchmark harness that measures stable-state throughput and tail latencies (p95/p99) across core model variants and quantization profiles. This ticket covers: design of stepped workloads (ramp, sustain, cooldown), sequence-length distributions (short/mid/long), KV cache warm/cold scenarios, jitter injection, and automated regression detection logic that integrates with CI and alerting. Deliverables: 1) a reusable Go/TS harness component that runs in CI and on dedicated perf runners, 2) standardized benchmark definitions (YAML) for each core model, 3) a regression detector that computes relative TPS and p95 deltas, flags regressions based on configurable thresholds, and creates alerts/PR comments when triggered, 4) dashboards and saved queries in Console for historical comparison, 5) documentation for running locally and interpreting results.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs synthetic stepped-load profiles and outputs CSV/JSON with tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and per-request metadata.
CI job (bench/tps/daily) runs without flakiness >= 5 consecutive runs and posts metrics to console and GH PR comments.
Regression detector raises an alert when TPS drops by >=5% or p95 increases by >=15% compared to baseline with configurable windowing.
Bench definitions exist for short (<=64 tokens), medium (128-512 tokens) and long (>1024 tokens) workloads and for cold/warm KV cache states.
Docs include runbook for triaging a detected regression, linking to flamegraphs, run artifacts, and suggested rollbacks/mitigations.
comments: 2025-02-10 Maya Kline: Initial spec written — focused on reproducibility and CI integration. Proposed thresholds: 5% TPS drop, 15% p95 increase. Asked Eng to validate noise floor and SLO-window sizing.
2025-02-11 Arjun Patel: Prototype runner implemented (go bench runner). It emits per-request timestamps and token counts. Still need sequence-length sampler and KV cache toggles.

2025-02-12 Arjun Patel: Ran first smoke against small test cluster (gpu-dev-2). Observed high variance for long-sequence runs; suspected interference from background autoscaler. Added pod isolation to perf runner.
2025-02-13 Priya Rao (SRE): Suggested adding a control baseline that runs a stable pinned commit to account for infra noise. Also recommended storing raw traces in artifacts/GCS for post-mortem.

2025-02-14 Arjun Patel: Implemented stepped-load profile (ramp 0->100 req/s over 60s, sustain 10m, cooldown 60s) and three sequence length samplers. Added KV cache cold/warm toggle using a prefill endpoint.

2025-02-15 QA: Integration test matrix run against runtime-1.18-stable: short/med/long, cold/warm cache. Results attached as CSV in PR. Short and med stable; long still noisy. Plan: increase sustained window for long to 30m and add jitter smoothing.

2025-02-16 Arjun Patel: Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2048 . Added regression detector service that consumes bench JSON and computes delta against a daily baseline. Detector posts results to GH PR comments and creates Slack ops alerts.
2025-02-17 Product review (Lena Brooks): Agreed thresholds for gating Dedicated rollouts. Request: expose per-model quantization labels in outputs so PM can filter regressions by quant profile.
2025-02-18 Arjun Patel: Added dashboard links and CI job definition. Next: nail down stable baseline selection algorithm and run longer windows for long-sequence matrix.
FOLLOW-UP: schedule a 1-hour triage playbook session with SRE and runtime team to define rollback steps and canary gating based on bench signals.
runbook_snippet: Run locally: ./bin/bench-runner --profile=stepped --model=rwkv-small --duration=10m --seq-dist=medium --kv-cache=warm. Output JSON saved to ./out.json. Upload using ./tools/upload-bench ./out.json.
test_matrix: long: seq>1024, sustained=30m, baseline_commit=runtime-1.17 (pinned for stability)
